newsitem.title: SPAIN: BoS to keep rate unchanged at repo - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: BoS to keep rate unchanged at repo - Reuter poll.

text.p: The Bank of Spain is expected to leave unchanged its official key money market rate at its regular repurchase agreement operation on Thursday, a survey of 10 financial experts showed on Wednesday.
Eight of those polled ruled out a quick move, while the remaining two gave a 50 percent probability to a fresh reduction in the 6.25 percent cost of bank refunding on Thursday.

For the majority, December CPI inflation, which undershot the government's public target of 3.4 percent to end the year at 3.2 percent year-on-year, was not low enough to prompt the central bank into another reduction.
"I don't expect the Bank of Spain will cut the rate tomorrow..they'd rather wait for the next data," said Carmen Alcaide, economist at the Banco Bilbao Vizcaya.
The peseta, having broken the 84.00 level versus the mark last week, was considered a factor which could prod the Bank of Spain towards an early move.
"But the peseta is a little weaker today. We'll see where it closes, but I do not see any big pressure," Alcaide said.
In 1996, the Bank of Spain cut the official rate seven times to 6.25 percent from nine pct in January. The latest reduction of 50 basis points was on December 13.
